evidence: DESIGN (source) - no structural defect found for this row. (1) Reward shaping: task tests/scoring.toml = gates render/constraints 0.0, weights functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, floors functional 0.05; tools/score.py identical to template (weighted mean of dimension scores, gates and floor only zero the reward). (2) Functional has 43 independently scored binary criteria, total weight 58.5, weights 0.5-2.5 (no criterion above 2.5/58.5 = 4.3%); prompt.md line 13 orders 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures ... A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles', and line 13/39 give fallbacks when setup fails (new job of your own; Tomas seeded conversation if hro_candidate_linked fails), so one failed feature does not cascade. (3) Polish: 5 binary criteria weights 3,3,2,1.5,2.5 (total 12) on distinct concerns (live board preservation, live thread preservation, earlier-load anchoring, failed send, session end). (4) Visual: 5 likert points=5 criteria with described anchors 1-5 (weight 1.2 each), so craft is graded, not pass/fail. (5) The only shared preconditions are the gates (sign-in; create job + candidate seen from an independent Observer context) and the identical in-dimension gate in each scored prompt; these exclude dead/static apps (check 39) and any real multi-user app clears them, so they do not collapse partial-quality apps. ILLUSTRATIVE SPREAD (computed from frozen weights, not measured): an otherwise complete app with no push updates loses hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_counts, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_seen -> functional 0.838 and polish <=0.5 (the two 3-weight live rows); a basic single-board CRUD app passing only open/add/email/one-stage/arrive/reorder/reject/reject-hired/reopen/notes/restart -> functional 0.188, reward ~0.25 with weak polish/visual; the golden-quality app -> near 1. That is a graded, monotone-looking spread. MEASUREMENT GAP (why not Pass): raw-evidence-index.json scope states verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; its only artifacts are a scripted golden Playwright/API driver (workspace.cjs, results/workspace.json, screenshots), which is not a configured judge run and has no weak/mutated-app scores. REVIEW_POLICY.md requires a hash-bound reward-discrimination record before local clearance, and the skill forbids upgrading an unmeasured claim to Pass. Hence Not exercised, risk=true. RESIDUAL RISKS to watch when measuring: (a) Workload collapse: the functional judge has one 9000 s budget (template-canonical) for a 13-protocol walk with many independent contexts and 15 s waits; prompt line 53 maps budget exhaustion to binary 0 'NOT EXERCISED' per unobserved row, so a run that times out late (protocols A, D) compresses scores irrespective of app quality, and a total rewardkit timeout (test.sh line 224, 11100 s) yields no scored reward. No full configured judge duration has been measured. (b) Shared replay precondition: 10 criteria require replaying a captured HTTP request (hro_interview_full, hro_observer_readonly, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_anonymous, hro_stale_refused, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places, hro_undo_conflict, hro_undo_once, hro_candidate_private = 16.5/58.5 = 28% of functional); prompt line 17 limits replay to 'page.evaluate fetch or context request' of a route the UI used. An app whose mutations travel over a WebSocket (hireops_rules.md:123 allows sockets for live updates; mutation transport is not mandated) could lose that block together; this is a check-27/6 concern more than a discrimination collapse, and the remaining 72% still grades, so it is recorded as a residual risk, not a Fail. (c) Floor cliff: functional must exceed 0.05 (>2.925 weight), so an app passing the gates but fewer than ~3 weight of rows scores 0 overall; template-controlled and intended (check 43), noted only. Adversarial attempts: a plausible broken app that could pass with a high score - none found from source, because each weighted row needs its own positive control and server refusal by replay; a conforming alternative that could fail broadly - only the WebSocket-mutation variant in (b) and the timeout variant in (a), both unmeasured.
